Introduction

What Is a Trust?

A Trust is a legal arrangement where a settlor transfers property or assets to trustees, who hold and manage them for the benefit of specified beneficiaries or a defined purpose. Private trusts are governed by the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, while public charitable and religious trusts fall under applicable state Public Trust Acts.

Trusts are commonly used for charitable work, religious institutions, and family or estate planning, each with somewhat different registration and compliance requirements.

Weigh Your Options

Advantages & Disadvantages

Advantages

  • Well suited to charitable, religious or estate planning purposes
  • Assets are managed under a clear legal framework for beneficiaries
  • Tax exemptions available for registered charitable trusts, subject to conditions
  • Trust deed can be tailored to the settlor's specific intentions

Disadvantages

  • Trust deed terms are generally difficult to alter once executed
  • Trustees carry significant fiduciary responsibility
  • State-specific rules can add complexity for public trusts
  • Not a fit for a commercial, profit-distributing business

Eligibility

Who Can Form a Trust

  • A settlor capable of contracting, who transfers property to the trust
  • At least two trustees for most public charitable trusts (requirements vary by state)
  • A clearly defined charitable, religious or private purpose
  • Identifiable beneficiaries or a defined class of beneficiaries

Step-by-Step

Registration Process & Timeline

1. Draft the Trust Deed

We draft a deed setting out the trust's objects, trustees, beneficiaries and governance terms.

2. Execute on Stamp Paper

The deed is signed by the settlor and trustees, and executed on stamp paper of the applicable value.

3. Registration with the Sub-Registrar

The trust deed is registered with the local Sub-Registrar of Assurances.

4. PAN & Tax Registrations

Apply for the trust's PAN and, where applicable, 12A and 80G registration for tax exemption. Timelines can vary by state and case.

Required Documents

What You'll Need

  • PAN and address proof of the settlor and trustees
  • Passport-size photographs of settlor and trustees
  • Proof of the registered address of the trust
  • Trust deed on appropriate stamp paper

Annual Compliance

Ongoing Requirements

  • Income tax return filing for the trust
  • Audit of accounts, where required under tax exemption provisions
  • Maintaining records of income application towards the trust's objects
  • Renewal or compliance filings tied to 12A/80G registration, where applicable
